q22.text: How would you connect our Customer Journey Analytics data to AI assistant traffic, and what do you need from us?

lines: C01: Connect Brand Visibility and CJA measurement [one-time]
C06: Audiences that act on the data [one-time]
CJ03: Adobe Analytics upgrade to CJA [one-time]
sections: Brand Visibility sends aggregate AI-agent activity (from CDN logs, by URL and host) into CJA through an Experience Platform source. AI-referred visits and conversions come from CJA's own web data, and Brand Visibility reads those results for its business impact view.

Four separate measures. AI-agent activity (from CDN logs) and monitored visibility (tracked prompts) are what Brand Visibility adds; AI-referred visits and conversions come from your CJA web data, which ordinary referrer reporting can show without it; lift comes only from a test. The data is aggregate: nothing ties a person to an AI mention.

We will configure the supported ABV bot-data connection and map URLs and hosts; identify AI-referred visits in the existing CJA web data with a derived field on AI referring domains; and align observed AI-referral and conversion measures with existing CJA data.

We will define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with you how each audience is used in its existing channels.
We will plan the upgrade path, implement Web SDK alongside the Analytics source connector for history, port reporting API use and exports, and migrate projects and components.
draft.plain:
Our approach
- Brand Visibility sends aggregate AI-agent activity (from CDN logs, by URL and host) into CJA through an Experience Platform source. AI-referred visits and conversions come from CJA's own web data, and Brand Visibility reads those results for its business impact view.
- Four separate measures. AI-agent activity (from CDN logs) and monitored visibility (tracked prompts) are what Brand Visibility adds; AI-referred visits and conversions come from your CJA web data, which ordinary referrer reporting can show without it; lift comes only from a test. The data is aggregate: nothing ties a person to an AI mention.

What we would do
- We will configure the supported ABV bot-data connection and map URLs and hosts; identify AI-referred visits in the existing CJA web data with a derived field on AI referring domains; and align observed AI-referral and conversion measures with existing CJA data.
- We will define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with you how each audience is used in its existing channels.
- We will plan the upgrade path, implement Web SDK alongside the Analytics source connector for history, port reporting API use and exports, and migrate projects and components.

sells: The paid Brand Visibility offering, not the free trial (CJA's page requires it for the source)
asks: CDN access logs forwarded to and received by Brand Visibility for each site, and Adobe's confirmation that the site is available in the source
An Experience Platform user who sets up the Adobe Brand Visibility source dataflow in the sandbox used by the CJA connection; each site can be allocated to one dataflow only
A CJA administrator who adds the Brand Visibility dataset to a connection on that sandbox and its fields to a data view; Adobe's managed connector stops at the Experience Platform dataset
A full URL field in the web event dataset that matches Brand Visibility's CDN URL, for the page join
A CJA derived field that groups AI referring domains, for referral analysis inside CJA (CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate; derived fields are not in CJA Foundation)

q27.text: Our marketing team runs Marketo Engage. How would site forms on the new site feed Marketo, and what licensing does that need?

lines: XB09: Site forms that submit to Marketo [one-time]
MK05: User training and setup documentation [one-time]
sections: Forms built with AEM Forms in the Universal Editor for Edge Delivery pages can use the Submit to Marketo Engage action; submissions run through AEM Publish, and AEM Forms needs its own license.
Lead forms built with AEM Forms on Edge Delivery pages submit to Marketo Engage through AEM Publish, ready for scoring and nurture.
We will build the lead forms in Universal Editor, configure the Submit to Marketo Engage action with field mapping to Marketo, and test that submissions create or update leads.
We will train the marketing users on programs, smart campaigns and templates, and document the new instance setup so the team can run it after launch.
We will run the go-live checklist, cut over DNS and the CDN, verify Brand Visibility, analytics, redirects and forms on the live site, and support your team for two weeks after launch.
Each month we will review Admin, Marketing Activities, Design Studio and Database for clean-up, deliverability and scoring changes, and agree the fixes with your Marketo owner.
draft.plain:
Our approach
- Forms built with AEM Forms in the Universal Editor for Edge Delivery pages can use the Submit to Marketo Engage action; submissions run through AEM Publish, and AEM Forms needs its own license.
- Lead forms built with AEM Forms on Edge Delivery pages submit to Marketo Engage through AEM Publish, ready for scoring and nurture.

What we would do
- We will build the lead forms in Universal Editor, configure the Submit to Marketo Engage action with field mapping to Marketo, and test that submissions create or update leads.
- We will train the marketing users on programs, smart campaigns and templates, and document the new instance setup so the team can run it after launch.
- We will run the go-live checklist, cut over DNS and the CDN, verify Brand Visibility, analytics, redirects and forms on the live site, and support your team for two weeks after launch.

After launch
- Each month we will review Admin, Marketing Activities, Design Studio and Database for clean-up, deliverability and scoring changes, and agree the fixes with your Marketo owner.
